chapter: Streetcar, Cab revival shows and trips abroad
title: Boxing with Marlon Brando backstage at the Barrymore Theater
summary: Barefield set up a gym in the basement, where Brando boxed with him until a stagehand broke Brando's nose. He also recalls Ralph Meeker, Jack Palance and Anthony Quinn, whom he taught saxophone.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So anyway, we stayed -- was over there two years, and during that period we was there, well, Marlon Brando was --

wanted to be a boxer, you know. So I had -- since I had my boxing experience, we set up a gym in the basement of the Barrymore Theater, and we used to go down there and box between -- between scenes, because sometimes we'd have 15 minutes off, a half hour, if we have to -- we got time -- time to get back in the dressing room. And we had everything timed, so we could go have this time.

So we used to go in the basement and box between us. So they had to take that, had to stop it, because Marlon Brando would come on the stage so out of breath that he couldn't speak his lines. So Jessica Tandy protested. But before that, you know, he was -- Marlon was a very strong guy. He was strong. But he didn't know nothing about boxing. He had big arms and everything.

And he used to slug away at me, you know, and I'd say, Now look, take it easy, because if you box with somebody that doesn't know what -- what it's about and you hit them and they won't know how to protect -- they might get mad and hurt you. So soon enough, one day he put on the gloves with the stage hand, and this guy was about 6'3", and Marlon like a little bull, you know. And when this guy came in there and come in, Marlon ducked down, and he throwed one of them overhand rights, and he hit this guy and knocked him down.
Well, the guy got mad, jumped up and throwed a one-two at Marlon Brando, and Marlon caught the first one, but he

didn't know two was coming and opened up his hands and set one right back on the nose and broke his nose, flattened his nose right out. So he was out of the show for about, oh, six weeks until that --
Well, at this time Meeker, I think Ralph Meeker took his place. And then when he finally left the show, Jack Palance took his place.

Yeah. And I was given -- no, Anthony Quinn. Jack Palance also took his place on one stint, but Anthony Quinn came in the show, and I was giving him saxophone lessons between shows. He was trying to play the soprano saxophone.

And then, so, but we had a nice, nice two years with this show, Marlon Brando, and I remember we were right next to the Strand Theater, and Basie's band used to come into the Strand and -- I'd have -- well, between this time we'd always go over and hang out with Basie and then Billie Holiday would come up and all that.
